evidence.note: Environment recon then storage.py written as a foundation before task decomposition — foundational layer front-loaded.

Explicit decomposition into 8 subsystem tasks via TaskCreate, ordered dependency-aware: SigV4 first, then core object CRUD, then multipart/copy (which depend on CRUD), then versioning/tagging, then cross-cutting CORS/lifecycle/policy/notifications, then admin+console API, then console UI, then audit. All ~dozen subsystems enumerated; none left orphaned.

Tasks cycled through in_progress→completed states as each milestone was finished and verified — genuine milestone tracking, but descriptions are scope statements rather than explicit written acceptance checks.
Extended reactive debugging of server startup/env vars did not reshape or revise the milestone plan; the decomposition was created upfront and not treated as a living, revised plan.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it enumerates all major subsystems and sequences them in a genuinely dependency-aware order with foundational risk (SigV4, storage) explicitly front-loaded and dependents (multipart, versioning, console UI) placed after their prerequisites. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the per-milestone 'done-checks' are scope descriptions rather than explicit acceptance criteria written into each milestone, and the plan was created upfront and marked complete rather than being a living plan revised as scope reality emerged. This places it at 7 — between the sensible-ordering (5) and explicit-hierarchy-with-acceptance-checks (8) anchors.
